thread.title: Stock Market Update: From Green to Red

title: Stock Market Update: From Green to Red
text:
From Green to Red 30-Apr-18 12:55 ET Dow -35.41 at 24275.78, Nasdaq -49.50 at 7070.30, S&P -12.73 at 2657.18
[BRIEFING.COM] The stock market began today's session modestly higher, but a recent bout of selling has pulled the S&P 500 into the red; the benchmark index is currently down 0.5%, hovering at its session low. Meanwhile, the Dow and the Nasdaq are down 0.1% and 0.7%, respectively.
10 of 11 S&P 500 sectors are currently trading in negative territory. The telecom services group (-1.3%) is the worst performer after Sprint (S 5.51, -0.99, -15.2%) and T-Mobile (TMUS 59.89, -4.63, -7.2%) agreed to an all-stock merger that values the combined company at $146 billion. The health care sector (-0.8%) is also showing relative weakness, with Allergan (AGN 155.73, -6.31, -3.9%) down despite better-than-expected first quarter earnings, and Celgene (CELG 85.49, -5.69, -6.2%) lower after Morgan Stanley said a re-filing for Celgene's multiple sclerosis drug ozanimod may take over a year.
On the upside, the consumer discretionary sector (-0.2%) is showing relative strength after McDonald's (MCD 166.00, +7.69, +4.9%) reported upbeat earnings and revenues for Q1. The financial space (-0.1%) also outperforms, and the energy group (+0.2%) is the lone advancer as crude oil rallies; WTI crude futures are up 0.7% at $68.56/bbl, overcoming overnight losses of around 1.0%.
Elsewhere, Apple (AAPL 165.21, +2.89, +1.8%) has rebounded today, but the top-weighted technology sector (-0.5%) can't keep ahead of the broader market. Similarly, Walmart (WMT 88.51, +1.22, +1.4%) is up after announcing Sainsbury's, but the consumer staples sector (-0.6%) underperforms.
